back: Small-scale activities not registered or fully regulated, such as vending and backyard workshops, usually without contracts or social protection.

front: Describe two trends in employment in Zimbabwe since the 2000s.
back: Formal jobs fell as firms closed; the informal sector grew; youth unemployment and underemployment are high; many workers emigrated.

front: Give two benefits of the informal sector.
back: Jobs and incomes for people without formal work; easy to enter; cheap goods; builds business skills.

front: Give two problems of the informal sector.
back: Low, irregular incomes; no pensions or sick pay; little tax paid; hard to get loans; poor conditions.
Self-employment, hiring workers, and linkages that create jobs at suppliers.
A policy of increasing the share of businesses and resources owned and controlled by local citizens.

front: When is indigenisation most likely to create jobs?
back: When it helps local people start and expand new businesses, not only when ownership of existing firms is transferred.

front: List the parts of a small project plan.
back: Idea and market; resources and capital; costs; price and revenue; profit and break-even; marketing; risks; records.

front: Break-even quantity for a small project = ?
back: Equipment (fixed) cost ÷ (price per unit − cost per unit).
